title: Free characteristic criterion and normal crossings boundary
statement: Let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $U$ be its triviality locus. For every geometric point $\bar x$ above $x\in X$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is regular if and only if $\overline M_{\bar x}\cong\mathbf N^r$ for some finite $r\geq0$. If these equivalent conditions hold everywhere, then $X$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], $U$ is open dense in $X$, and $D=(X\setminus U)_{\rm red}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is an effective Cartier divisor: locally its ideal is generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism] at each point $D$ is cut out by a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters. This is a normal crossings divisor, allowing the empty divisor and allowing self-intersections of its global components.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: At a fixed geometric point use the sharp local algebra preparation to obtain A, P, I, r, their strict-henselization presentation and the hypotheses of the monoidal local regularity criterion. Apply that criterion. Enumerate the finite set of additive irreducibles by Fin n. Its two equivalences identify regularity of A with Nonempty(P=N^r). A free presentation of any rank s has s=r by the rank clause of the preparation, so the right-hand side is equivalent to existence of a finite free presentation.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: Strict-henselization regularity invariance identifies regularity of the ordinary stalk with that of A, giving the first clause at every geometric point. Under the everywhere-free hypothesis apply it to a geometric point above each ordinary point, obtained from an algebraic closure of its residue field. All ordinary stalks are regular; together with the existing local Noetherianity this is IsRegularScheme.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: For each ordinary point x choose such a geometric point and apply the one-chart boundary lemma using freeness there. This supplies an etale chart W_x with a point over x, a dense open V_x which is the inverse image of U, and reduced normal crossings complement. These charts cover X.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: Etale charts are open by the flat locally-finitely-presented openness theorem. Thus U is the union of the open images e_x(V_x), hence is open. For any nonempty open O of X choose x in O; its inverse image in W_x contains the chosen point and is nonempty open, so it meets dense V_x. Its image lies in O intersect U. This proves density, also vacuously for empty X.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4 and 1.7, printed pp. 69--70; Expose VIII, 3.4.4, printed p. 110, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117. Normal crossings here is the etale-local parameter criterion, not strictness of global components.

proof.text: Put Z=X minus U. Its inverse image closed subset is W_x minus V_x. Reduced Cartier descent on the jointly surjective etale family proves invertibility of the vanishing ideal of Z. The reduced-pullback isomorphism in that same descent theorem identifies its pullback ideal with the vanishing ideal of each inverse-image complement: take the kernels of the commuting closed-immersion maps and use invariance under isomorphism. Pull the parameter witness at the chosen point from the local normal crossings condition and compose its etale map with W_x->X. Functoriality of ideal pullback gives exactly the global normal crossings equation.
